seo.title: Karmic tail 21 4 19 compatibility: The World, The Emperor, The Sun
seo.description: Karmic tail 21 4 19 compatibility: a couple's own world, the rules that hold it and the Sun as the main task, read through Akhenaten and Nefertiti.

title: Karmic tail 21-4-19 in compatibility: the couple that builds its own world under one sun
short: The couple's tail 21-4-19 runs in a strange order. It opens with The World, the card of wholeness and completion, and sets The Sun, the simplest of all happinesses, as the main task. The couple starts where others finish: with the dream of a whole world for two (21). The road to the task runs through the laws, roles and order that keep that world standing (4, The Emperor). And what the two have to learn is a light that reaches both of them directly, not through a rulebook, a shop window or one person in charge (19). Almost three and a half thousand years ago one couple lived exactly this way. Akhenaten and Nefertiti built a city on empty land, carved its laws into the cliffs and made the sun their faith.

sections.h2: A city made by desire: The World at the entry to the task
paragraphs: In the fifth year of his reign Amenhotep IV does what few couples dare: he leaves the old house completely. He takes the name Akhenaten and chooses for his new capital an empty bay of desert on the east bank of the Nile, roughly halfway between Thebes and Memphis. The boundary stelae carved into the cliffs around this land declare that it was "not being the property of a god, not being the property of a goddess, not being the property of a ruler". The city was named Akhetaten, "Horizon of the Aten". At the top of the stelae the royal family worships the sun, and beside many of them statues of the king, the queen and their daughters were cut from the same rock.

The queen's name, Nefertiti, means "the beautiful one has come". There is no better opening scene for the tail 21-4-19: two people arrive on land where no one's rules apply and decide to build everything on it.

The entry to the task is what the couple wants together: its shared wishes and agreements, its "common language". In this tail the common language is The World. Couples like this recognise themselves by their first years. Six months after meeting, a house that does not exist yet is already sketched on a café napkin. The two move somewhere nobody knows them: "let's start from a clean page". They have their own cooking, their own private words, their own idea of how to live, and friends call them the perfect couple. Benebell Wen calls The World "the card of synthesis" and notes that it is "considered the best card in the tarot deck": everything has come together into one whole.

The Great Hymn to the Aten, carved in the tomb of the courtier Ay, tells how the world came to be: the sun made it "according to thy desire, whilst thou wert alone" (in John A. Wilson's translation). The line could stand as an epigraph to the entry of this tail. Here the world is born of desire, and the couple's entry is the point of desire too. Yet the second half of the line shows where the entry resists: a world made by the desire of one is handed to the other ready-made.

The entry sits on the line of tasks, so the same wish also brakes. A whole world is hard to keep open. An old friend stops coming round: he "doesn't fit". One partner's hobby that has no place in the shared philosophy becomes a joke at the dinner table. One person's views quietly become "our views", though nobody ever voted on them. The relatives are shown a finished world instead of being asked for advice. Each year looks like the last one, because the last one was right. Wen writes of The World reversed as a person who is "consciously and knowingly in denial", "remaining willfully ignorant". A perfect world does not like news.

sections.h2: Laws carved in rock: The Emperor in the middle of the task
paragraphs: A world once built has to be held. In Akhetaten this was done literally. The city's limits were marked by sixteen stelae cut into the cliffs on both sides of the valley: a territory 20–25 km across the river and 13 km from south to north. The stelae carry decrees on where the temples will stand and where the tombs will be. "Let a tomb be made for me in the eastern mountain of Akhetaten", and right after it, an order that the Great King's Wife Nefertiti and the King's Daughter Meritaten be buried there. The king swears not to expand the city beyond its southern and northern stelae. For a long time this oath was read as a vow never to leave the city; the archaeologists of the Amarna Project explain that it banned extending the borders, not the king's travels. Still, the main point is plain: a family that had only just arrived on empty land at once wrote into stone where it would lie.

Lisovskaya's book gives the middle of a couple's tail no meaning of its own; it is an addition to the main task. Our reading: the middle shows what the couple goes through on its way from the wish to the task. Here it goes through The Emperor. Wen writes that with this card "themes of order, authority, and jurisdiction will be at play". A boundary stela is jurisdiction carved in stone.

For a 21-4-19 couple this is the time of the constitution. A budget spreadsheet with colour-coded columns appears. They settle who handles the money, whose parents they visit for the holidays, when the lights go out, whether phones are allowed at the table. At first every rule protects the shared world from chaos. Then a rule made in the first year is still obeyed in the fifth, and nobody remembers why. Among the tasks of this energy in a couple Lisovskaya names exactly this: do not create rules that get in the way later.

The second plot of the middle is who holds the sceptre. On one block from Amarna, found at Hermopolis, Nefertiti stands on the royal barge and raises her arm to strike a captive. That pose belonged to the king alone. For Egypt it was unusual; for a couple it is an ordinary evening: two people, and each has a ready answer about the right way to do things. The struggle for first place goes on without shouting — through "it's already decided", through silence, through a face that will not say whether it is joy or anger. What has to be learned is the one thing The Emperor cannot do: to talk about feelings before talking about rules.

sections.h2: The sun with hands: the main task, 19
paragraphs: Akhenaten's new faith set one god above all others: the Aten, the visible disc of the sun. Across the country the name of Amun was hacked off the walls. The sun god used to be drawn as a man with a falcon's head. In Amarna the sun became a circle whose rays end in human hands. On the house altar in the Berlin museum those hands hold out symbols of life to the king and the queen. A sun with hands is an image both generous and unsettling: hands give, but hands also hold.

The hymn to the Aten ends with words about who owns this light: "You are in my heart, There is no other who knows you, Only your son", followed by Akhenaten's royal name (in Miriam Lichtheim's translation). Ordinary people received the sun through the royal family. The Berlin slab with the king, the queen and three daughters beneath the rays of the disc is a house altar: such altars stood in people's homes. The light reached them reflected, through a portrait of a happy couple.

The main task of a couple's tail is read mostly through its minus: what the couple fails at and what it has to learn. The Sun in its plus is a couple you can see from far away: bright, warm, successful, both with a standing of their own. In love readings Wen is direct about The Sun: "It indicates a radiant marriage, perhaps one to a spouse with a successful career", and "It could suggest a power couple". The Amarna pair was a power couple in the most literal sense: on the reliefs the two of them rule together, worship together and hold their children together. But the task of the tail 21-4-19 is not to shine. It is about whose light it is.

The minus of The Sun in this couple shows in scenes. One of the two becomes the person who knows "what makes us happy", and the couple's happiness starts to pass through that person's approval. The other's victory is called "ours", and can no longer be called by its owner's name. Comparisons creep in: whose holiday was brighter, whose couple looks happier in photos. Or the other way round: the light goes into work and status, and at home only the reflected kind remains — a story about how well everything is going. Difficulties go unspoken, because the sun must not set; the hymn knows this too: "When you have dawned they live, When you set they die". Care holds out its hands and does not take them back when the other wants to manage alone.

Waite writes that The Sun signifies "the transit from the manifest light of this world, represented by the glorious sun of earth, to the light of the world to come, which goes before aspiration and is typified by the heart of a child". Akhenaten prayed to precisely the glorious sun of earth — the disc you could see in the sky and on every wall. The main task of a 21-4-19 couple is that very transit: from the sun the neighbours can see to the light a child knows.

sections.h2: What Waite put in The Emperor's hand
paragraphs: On Waite's classic card The Emperor holds a sceptre shaped like the crux ansata, the looped cross, that is, the Egyptian ankh, the sign of life: "He has a form of the Crux ansata for his sceptre and a globe in his left hand." Wen sees the same thing: "a scepter, one that is reminiscent of an ankh". In Amarna this sign was held not by kings but by the rays of the sun: the hands of the Aten held the ankh out to the faces of the king and queen.

Put side by side, the two pictures give the key piece of evidence for this tail. The Emperor in the middle holds what The Sun of the main task hands him. Our reading: this couple's order is legitimate as long as it passes life on. Once the sceptre starts to think of itself as the source of light, the budget, the roles and the rules serve no longer the home, but themselves.

Waite's second piece of evidence sits in the entry of the tail. In every 21-4-19 couple The World at the entry is made of The Lovers and The Devil (6 + 15; see the calculation). Waite describes the two figures of The Lovers "as if Adam and Eve when they first occupied the paradise of the earthly body", and the two chained to The Devil "as if Adam and Eve after the Fall". The World, in the first part of his book, is "the soul's intoxication in the earthly paradise". The couple's entry is made of paradise before the expulsion and paradise after it, and the sum is paradise again — only this time built with their own hands. Hence its strength, and hence its walls.

sections.h2: The Window of Appearance: how the circle of tail 21-4-19 turns
paragraphs: The palace at Amarna had a window where the king and queen showed themselves to the court: the Window of Appearance. One scene recurs in the tombs of Akhetaten's officials: the royal couple at the window hand out gold collars, and below, those being honoured receive them. It appears in Ay's tomb too, the very tomb where the hymn is carved, and Ay himself later became pharaoh. The sun in the window showers gold: the light has turned into a spectacle and a reward.

The circle of the tail turns like this. The couple wants a whole world and builds it (21). To keep that world from falling apart, it writes laws and divides power (4). Little by little the laws eat up the simple light. Joy gets displayed in the window — to the relatives, to friends, in the feed — while at home it is handed out as gifts and as praise for good behaviour. Hard things go unsaid: admitting a difficulty feels like admitting the sun has set. When the air gets stuffy, the couple wants a new world: a move, a renovation, a second home, a new joint venture. New land with nobody else's rules, and everything starts over. A new city instead of a conversation.

Among her recommendations for The World, Lisovskaya advises a couple to go through difficulties together rather than run away from them. For the tail 21-4-19 this is the key to the circle: the next world will not solve the task the last one failed to solve, because the task is not in the world but in the sun.

sections.h2: The calculation: where Judgement hides in the tail 21-4-19
paragraphs: A couple's tail is calculated from two personal charts: each point of the couple is the sum of the same points of the two people, reduced to 22. Take the dates 08.01.1976 and 17.01.1976. The first has the personal karmic tail 6-20-14: The Lovers, Judgement, Temperance. The second has 15-20-5: The Devil, Judgement, The Hierophant. Both have 10, The Wheel of Fortune, in the centre of the chart.

The couple's centre: 10 + 10 = 20, Judgement. The middle of a couple's tail is not recalculated from the two outer numbers: it is the sum of the two personal middles. Here 21 + 19 also gives 40 → 4, but that is an arithmetic coincidence: apart from the middle, no number in this tail needed reducing.

Running every date through the site's engine shows that the example is no accident. The tail 21-4-19 occurs in roughly one couple in 476 (0.21%, 72nd of the 97 couple tails), and it is always built the same way: one partner has the personal tail 15-20-5, the other 6-20-14. So in every such couple:

ul: **The World at the entry is The Lovers plus The Devil.** One person's free choice and the other's attachment together make the wish for a whole world. This is no reason to sort the partners into "the chooser" and "the attached": in a couple, the sum is what works.

**The Sun in the main task is Temperance plus The Hierophant**, the two partners' personal karmic tasks. Waite calls Temperance "the analogy of solar light": it "tempers, combines and harmonises". The Hierophant for him is "the ruling power of external religion". The couple's sun is assembled from measure and from doctrine. Amarna chose doctrine and made the sun a state faith. A 21-4-19 couple has to assemble it from measure.
**The Emperor in the middle is Judgement plus Judgement.** Both partners have Judgement in the middle of their personal tails, and in the couple the two Judgements add up to power.

**The couple's centre is Judgement too, in 100% of such couples.** This is the atmosphere inside the couple, what lies between the two when nobody is watching. For Lisovskaya the key of this energy in a couple is family and kin: traditions, the parents' influence, the ability to forgive and to admit one's own mistakes, and in the minus, blame and silence about what one feels.

**The couple's values are one of the two halves of the entry:** The Devil in 52.9% of such couples, The Lovers in 47.1%. In the example above it is 15, The Devil. Lisovskaya ends her account of this energy with the thought that nobody belongs to anybody.

paragraphs: Three Judgements around The Emperor are strong evidence. Wen describes Judgement this way: "All evidence has been made available to the Seeker and the Seeker has rendered his or her judgment." Our reading: this couple judges a great deal — who is right, whose family lived the proper way, how things "ought to be done" — and the laws of the middle are built out of these verdicts. All the more reason for the main task: The Sun passes no verdicts. It shines.

The tail 21-4-19 never occurs as a personal tail. In a personal chart the entry of the tail equals the karmic task plus the centre of the chart, so for the entry to be 21 with a karmic task of 19 the centre would have to be 2, and no person has that centre. This story can only be born between two people.

Akhenaten died, and within a few years the court left his city. His heir Tutankhaten became Tutankhamun, putting the old god back into his name. The temples of the Aten were taken apart, and under Ramesses II their blocks were carried across the river to Hermopolis as fill for new buildings; that is how the block with Nefertiti in the king's pose survived. In the king list carved under Seti I at Abydos, Amenhotep III is followed directly by Horemheb: Akhenaten is not there. The world built by desire was dismantled stone by stone.

Yet two things from this city are kept in Berlin, and neither is about power. The first is that same house altar: beneath the rays of the Aten the king holds his eldest daughter and leans towards her as if to kiss her, while the queen has one girl on her lap and the youngest on her shoulder. The second is the bust of Nefertiti from the workshop of the sculptor Thutmose, found on 6 December 1912 by Ludwig Borchardt's expedition. In the excavation diary Borchardt wrote: "Beschreiben nützt nichts, ansehen" — "Description is useless, must be seen." The bust's left eye has no inlay. Borchardt had the workshop debris searched, even what had already been carted away, and some of it sifted; no eye turned up, and later he wrote: "Only much later did I realise that it had never existed."

Of a whole world, what survived was a kiss and an unfinished eye. For a 21-4-19 couple this is the answer to the main task. The Sun is not a project and not a shop window: you do not describe it, you look at it. Nor does it demand the completeness The World asks for at the entry.
Akhetaten's ending is known. A couple with this tail has no ending written in its cards: there is a task, and it is for the two of them to solve.

A strong couple with this tail looks like the Amarna pair without the guard at the window. Its world is large and open: travel, moves, a shared outlook on life with room for someone else's opinion. Its Emperor is a frame, not a prison: a budget, plans, an order that holds the house up for as long as people live in it. Its Sun is a light that reaches each of them directly. What changes the script:

ul: **A gate in the wall.** Something new keeps coming into the shared world: one partner's friend, the other's hobby, a town neither has seen. A world where nothing comes in turns into Groundhog Day very quickly.
**Rules in pencil.** Every rule the couple makes has a review date: "we'll try it for a year, then decide again". Stelae were cut into rock; a couple can make do with a note on the phone.
**Victory by name.** One partner's success is called by that partner's name, not "ours". Thanks go to something specific, not to everything being proper.
**Hard things in daylight.** A problem is raised calmly and in good time, without waiting for dark. Admitting a difficulty is not admitting the sun has set.
**Joy without an audience.** The couple keeps some joys that are shown to no one: not for a photo, not for the relatives, not as a gift. A sun that shines only in the window is a duty, not a sun.

paragraphs: In the hymn the sun made the world "whilst thou wert alone". In a 21-4-19 couple two people make the world, and this is its main difference from Amarna. The task is for the light to belong to both as well.

ul: **21 · The World — entry to the task.** The couple's shared language is the wish for wholeness: their own home, their own city, their own philosophy, a life where everything has come together. This wish is how the couple enters the task, and it is also what resists it: a whole world is hard to open to the outside.
**4 · The Emperor — middle of the task.** The road leads through structure: a budget, roles, rules, the question of who decides. Order holds the shared world up and easily turns into its walls.
**19 · The Sun — main task.** To learn a joy that reaches each of them directly: no window for an audience, no gift in place of a conversation, no single person who knows "what makes us happy".

intro: A couple's tail is not a forecast and not a verdict on the union. It is a task, written in three cards and in the way they are added up from two personal charts. What follows is an investigation: the evidence lies in the cards themselves, in the books and in the arithmetic of the tail.

faq.q: What does the karmic tail 21-4-19 mean in compatibility?
faq.a: It is the tail of a couple that enters its task wanting a whole world for two (21, The World), goes through it by way of laws, roles and order (4, The Emperor) and learns the main thing: a simple joy that reaches both partners directly (19, The Sun). The key point is The Sun: in its minus it means light put on display, victories taken over and silence about what is hard.

faq.q: Why is the middle of the tail 4 and not another number?
faq.a: The middle of a couple's tail is the sum of the two personal middles: in partners with this tail both are 20, Judgement, and 20 + 20 = 40 → 4. In this tail 21 + 19 also gives 40 → 4, but the rule of the calculation stays the same: the middle is never recalculated from the outer numbers.

faq.q: Can 21-4-19 be a personal karmic tail?
faq.a: No. In a personal chart the entry of the tail equals the karmic task plus the centre of the chart. For the entry to be 21 with a karmic task of 19, the centre would have to be 2, and no person has that centre. So 21-4-19 appears only in a couple's matrix.

faq.q: Are there couple tails made of the same numbers in another order?
faq.a: No. The first number of a couple's tail is always divisible by three, so of 21, 4 and 19 only 21 can open a tail, and the site's engine never finds the order 21-19-4 in any couple. The tail 21-4-19 is the only one of its kind.

faq.q: Is the tail 21-4-19 a bad sign for a couple?
faq.a: No. A couple's tail shows a task, not an outcome: it holds no events and no dates. The Sun is one of the brightest cards in the deck, and the task here is not to avoid misfortune but to let joy stop being a shop window and become something shared.

report.h3: Description is useless, must be seen

report: After Akhenaten's death the court left his city, the temples were broken up for stone, and his name dropped out of the king list at Abydos. Two things from Akhetaten are kept in Berlin, and neither is about power. A house altar: the king holds his eldest daughter and leans towards her as if to kiss her, while the queen has one girl on her lap and the youngest on her shoulder. A strong couple with this tail leaves a gate in the wall, writes its rules in pencil with a review date, calls a victory by the name of whoever won it, talks about hard things in daylight and keeps some joys without an audience.
